title: Excess and shortage
question: Mrs Tan has some sweets for her pupils. If she gives each pupil 5 sweets, she will be short of 24 sweets. If she gives each pupil 2 sweets, she will be short of 6 sweets. How many pupils are there?

relations.from: If she gives each pupil 5 sweets, she will be short of 24 sweets
If she gives each pupil 2 sweets, she will be short of 6 sweets

timeline.say: Mrs Tan has some sweets for her pupils. If she gives each pupil 5 sweets, she will be short of 24 sweets. If she gives each pupil 2 sweets, she will be short of 6 sweets. How many pupils are there?
Giving 5 sweets each, she is short of 24 sweets.
Giving 2 sweets each, she is short of only 6 sweets.
Pause and think. Why does the shortage get smaller?
The shortage drops by 24 minus 6, which is 18 sweets.
So there are 18 divided by 3, which is 6 pupils.
Let's check: both ways, Mrs Tan has 6 sweets. It works!
So, there are 6 pupils. Well done!
